items_missed: No agenda statement at the open — never told her what the call would cover or roughly how long it would take, and never asked 'sound good?'
Never checked or confirmed availability for a specific move date; only mentioned in passing at the end that 'as long as we have the availability on those days' it would be easy to book
Never said 'pricing is super simple' or gave the full what's-included list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, tools) — only covered pads/shrink wrap and no-fee assembly
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — no pre-move email with the mover's photo/info
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — no arrival-window discount language at all
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge)
Never said when the clock starts (on-site when the contract opens) — gave the 2.5 hr minimum and 15-min increments but not the start trigger

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill', no consolidation examples (toys, drawers, wall photos), no 'take a carload' tip. Closest gesture was splitting pack/move across two days 'so we're not cramming everything on one day'
Never named the number of trucks, walk distance, or additional stops; no equivalents/school-bus reference
No booking attempt — customer said 'I'm going to think about it' and he accepted without a single ask to lock in the date
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email, business hours, or how to reach the team
60 cents/lb competitor baseline not used when explaining No Worries coverage
Used her name roughly twice ('Nikki'), not 3+ times
top_strength: Outstanding inventory discovery and estimate transparency — he walked the home room by room, caught the standing-desk/disassembly question, and then openly explained why he was padding the sixth-floor elevator load from a 60/40 to a 50/50 split. He also proactively re-priced Sunday/Monday to save her money without being asked.
coaching_note: The estimate work is strong; the sale is where he's leaving points. Add Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee to the pricing block, run the Save Your Ass prep speech before quoting, and make an actual booking ask instead of ending on 'let me know' — he had a warm, sold customer and never asked for the date.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and self-deprecating — the 'straw that broke the camel's back' joke over two folding camp chairs landed and she played along, and he apologized cleanly when he misread her address.
